region: model-theoretic (shallow substrate: extensional / world-indexed / world-time-indexed fragments with generalized-quantifier NPs and an axiomatized counting interface)
summary: 140-line, theorem-free substrate library, byte-identical (md5 7aeee3df8893df71cb049746b561c4c9, empty diff) to shallow/MontagueFragment.v, and imported by nothing in the repository. Section AbstractCounting (lines 15-31) axiomatizes an abstract cardinality `size : (Entity->Prop)->nat` with two Section-level Axioms (extensionality, subset-monotonicity) and defines Barwise & Cooper-style counting determiners G_some / G_exactly_n / G_at_least_n / G_most. Module MontagueExtensional (36-83) re-declares Entity/size and the two axioms at module level, gives a two-constructor NP type (proper name as fun P => P e; quantified NP as determiner+CN), a one-constructor sentence type over Prop, every/some/no, and two bare example sentences `most dogs love Mary`, `at least two women love Mary`. Module MontagueIntensional (88-110) indexes by World only, declares a property-taking `seek : (Entity -> World -> Prop) -> Entity -> World -> Prop`, and defines `john_seeks_a_unicorn := seek Unicorn john`. Module MontagueWorldTime (115-138) sets Index := World*Time, I A := Index -> A, adds an accessibility relation R with Axiom R_refl and a Kripke-style `box` that varies the world along R and holds the time fixed. 0 Theorem/Lemma/Example statements; nothing is proved. Compiles cleanly with Coq 8.20.1. Two defects in the counting interface were re-verified in a fresh scratch file against the compiled .vo: (a) `Axiom` inside a Section is discharged as a global constant generalized over the Section Variables, so the module exports `size_subset : forall (Entity:Type) (size:(Entity->Prop)->nat) A B, (forall x, A x -> B x) -> size A <= size B` - a claim about EVERY function into nat - from which `False` follows under ClassicalEpsilon (Qed; assumptions exactly size_subset, constructive_indefinite_description, classic); (b) the constant function size := fun _ => 5 satisfies both axioms while making G_most refutable for all N,P, G_at_least_n 2 provable for all N,P, and G_some true of an empty intersection (Qed, closed under the global context), so the axioms pin down nothing about counting.

sources.citation: Montague, R. (1973). The Proper Treatment of Quantification in Ordinary English (reprint pp. 17-34; line numbers are of `pdftotext montague73.pdf -`). §1 lexicon: B_T = {John, Mary, Bill, ninety, he_n} (92), B_TV = {find, lose, eat, love, date, be, seek, conceive} (93), B_CN = {man, woman, park, fish, pen, unicorn, price, temperature} (95); S2/F0-F2: every / the / a-an are the only determiners (113-116). §2: Type = smallest set with e, t, <a,b>, <s,a> (350-352); A, I, J = entities, possible worlds, moments of time (398-399); D_e = A, D_t = {0,1}, D_<a,b> = D_b^{D_a}, D_<s,a> = D_a^{I x J} (406-409); interpretation <A,I,J,<=,F> with A,I,J nonempty and <= a linear ordering of J (413-416); extension at point of reference <i,j> (420-423); clause 7 quantifier semantics (448-450); clause 8: [box phi]^{A,i,j,g} = 1 iff phi = 1 for all i' in I and all j' in J, plus W/H tense clauses (452-460); Thomason note 9: box is 'necessarily always' (896). §3: f(A/B) = f(A//B) = <<s,f(B)>,f(A)> (503-506); T1(d) John -> j* = lambda P. P{^j} (535); T2 every/the/a (537-538); T4, T5 delta'(^beta') (551-554); meaning postulates (1)-(9) (630-642), in particular (5) subject-extensionality of seek (637) and (9) seek' = try-to'(^find') (641-642), discussed 660-666; d* reduction (687-696). §4 examples: every man walks = forall u[man'*(u) -> walk'*(u)] (719); John finds a unicorn (723); John seeks a unicorn de dicto seek'(^j, ^lambda P exists u[unicorn'*(u) and P{^u}]) vs de re exists u[unicorn'*(u) and seek'*(j,u)] (733-738).

Dowty, Wall & Peters (1981). Introduction to Montague Semantics (image-only PDF; line numbers are of the DjVu-OCR .txt sidecar). Ch. 3 p. 61 (txt 2934-2945): 'most', 'few', 'many' 'have no ready correspondents in predicate logic'; the book's fragment 'will consider only the quantifiers every, some, and the'. Ch. 5 p. 127 (txt 5250-5252): box phi is true iff phi is true 'with respect to all possible worlds, not just those standing in a certain relation to the actual one' - no accessibility relation; p. 129 (txt 5419-5421): the system is S5, 'essentially the one used by Montague in PTQ'; pp. 131-132 (txt 5465-5478): index <w,t>; two candidate readings of box, 'necessarily always' (all <w',t'>) vs 'necessarily now' (all <w',t>, t fixed); the book chooses the former 'because Montague also used this interpretation of the necessity operator in PTQ'. Ch. 6 (6-10) 'John is seeking a unicorn' (txt 5905). Ch. 7 pp. 185-186 (txt 7657-7672): every A/B functor applies to the intension of its B argument; seek and find 'are both interpreted as functions applying to the intensions of term phrases'. Ch. 7 pp. 215-217 (txt 8926-8953): S5/T5 and derivation (7-60)/(7-61) of the de dicto reading seek'(j, ^lambda Q exists x[unicorn'(x) and Q{x}]).

Barwise & Cooper (1981). Generalized Quantifiers and Natural Language. L&P 4 (line numbers of `pdftotext`). §1.5: ||More than half of N|| = {X subset E : X contains more than half of the Ns}, ||Most N|| = {X : X contains most Ns} (324-328); §2.1: numerical determiners, '3 men run' = at least three, '!3 men run' = exactly three (498-503). Not named anywhere in the Coq file, but it is the only source for G_most / G_at_least_n / G_exactly_n and for the two example sentences; listed so the counting section is not misattributed to PTQ or DWP.

definitions_mapped.coq: Section AbstractCounting: Variable Entity : Type; Variable size : (Entity->Prop)->nat; Axiom size_ext; Axiom size_subset (lines 15-23)
definitions_mapped.source: none in PTQ or DWP; the implicit set cardinality |X| behind Barwise & Cooper 1981 §1.5 / §2.1
definitions_mapped.note: Only extensionality and subset-monotonicity are assumed: no size(empty)=0, no size(singleton)=1, no additivity, no finiteness. Verified with `About size_subset` on the compiled module: the closed Section turns both Axioms into global constants `forall [Entity:Type] (size:(Entity->Prop)->nat) A B, ...`, i.e. assertions about EVERY function into nat. Scratch MontagueProbe.v (this session) proves `discharged_size_subset_False : False` (Qed; Print Assumptions lists exactly size_subset, constructive_indefinite_description, classic) by taking size A := if excluded_middle_informative (A tt) then 0 else 1 on unit. Consistent relative to bare CIC and plain `Classical` (a closed term cannot inspect a Prop), and no repo file imports ClassicalEpsilon/ClassicalDescription, so the hazard is latent but real. The same scratch file shows size := fun _ => 5 satisfies both axioms (Qed) while refuting G_most for all N,P.

definitions_mapped.source: Barwise & Cooper 1981: ||some|| (nonempty intersection), numerical determiners n / !n = at least n / exactly n (498-503), ||Most N|| / ||More than half of N|| (324-328)
definitions_mapped.note: G_most N P := size(N and P) > size(N and not P) is the |N cap P| > |N minus P| rendering of 'more than half'. PTQ's only determiners are every / the / a (S2, 113-116) and DWP's fragment explicitly restricts itself to every / some / the (txt 2943-2945), so none of this is Montague. G_some (1 <= size(N and P)) is a different object from `some` at line 70 (an existential); under the two axioms they are not interderivable (constant-size countermodel: G_some holds of the empty intersection).

determination_rationale: The evidentiary base is thin (no theorems), but every PTQ construct the file does encode - the I x J index space, intensions as functions from indices, generalized-quantifier NPs with the lambda P. P j lifting, T2-shaped determiners, T4 subject-predicate application - goes into Coq as plain shallow types and definitions with no encoding trick, and nothing in the file points to a Coq-imposed obstacle. The departures (property-taking seek, Kripke/time-fixed box, dropped time coordinate, dropped individual concepts) are elective simplifications or importations from other theories, not workarounds forced by the proof assistant: PTQ's own box is directly writable as `fun i => forall w' t', phi (w', t')`, and shallow/PTQ.v in the same repository shows that the omitted machinery (individual concepts, T1-T17, postulates, W/H, the §4 examples as theorems) also embeds directly. The one structure that had to be axiomatized rather than defined is cardinality of Prop-valued predicates over an abstract type, and that belongs to the unattributed Barwise & Cooper addition, not to PTQ; even there the difficulty is the choice of Prop-valued predicates over an opaque Entity, not a limit of Coq.

artifact_classes.description: Coq has no native cardinality on `Entity -> Prop`, so the counting determiners rest on an axiomatized abstract `size` (lines 17-23, 38-40). The axiomatization is too weak to recover Barwise & Cooper's arithmetic of |N cap P| (constant `size` satisfies it and makes `most` unsatisfiable - MontagueProbe.v, Qed), and because the Section discharges it over every `size` function it is refutable under ClassicalEpsilon (MontagueProbe.v, Qed) - a Coq-specific hazard with no counterpart in the set-theoretic source.

`size` and every lexical item are opaque Parameters (Print Assumptions on most_dogs_love_mary lists size, mary, loves, Entity, Dog; on john_seeks_a_unicorn lists seek, john, Unicorn; on box lists World, Time, R); `most_dogs_love_mary`, `at_least_two_women_love_mary`, `john_seeks_a_unicorn` and `box` cannot be evaluated even in a finite model, and Prop-valued predicates make `size` non-definable in the first place (which is exactly why the over-general axiom stays consistent without choice).

Montague's two-valued D_t = {0,1} (PTQ line 407) is rendered as Prop with no excluded middle in the file: `no N P := ~ some N P` (lines 73, 106, 134) is intuitionistic negation, and `G_some` (1 <= size) vs `some` (exists) are not provably interderivable; cardinality of an undecidable predicate is non-computable, which forces `size` to be a Parameter rather than a function. None of this bites here only because nothing is proved.

duplicate_note: shallow/MontagueFragment.v is byte-for-byte identical (diff empty; md5 7aeee3df8893df71cb049746b561c4c9 for both). The shallow copy is the canonical one: it is `Require Import`ed by 11 files (shallow/kratzer2.v, extras/Aspect.v, DonkeyScope.v, DowtyTense.v, FocusEven.v, Imperfective2.v, ImperfectiveParadox.v, PolydefiniteSemantics.v, PresuppositionProjection.v, dowty_roles.v, kratzer_1977.v), whereas `grep -rn 'Require[^.]*\bMontague\b' --include='*.v'` finds no importer of extras/Montague.v. Both are listed in _CoqProject (lines 11 and 37); extras/Montague.v is dead weight and could be dropped from the build with no effect. shallow/PTQ.v (the other listed candidate, _CoqProject line 12) is NOT a duplicate: it is a 972-line hybrid deep/shallow formalization of PTQ proper (analysis trees, T1-T17, individual concepts, W/H, meaning postulates, §4 examples, 9 Theorem statements with 8 Qed and 1 Admitted - temperature_puzzle at line 837, 11 Axioms) that neither imports this file nor contains any of its counting / R / box material; PTQ.v is the far better PTQ formalization and this file is a substrate library. Verdict on the pair [Montague.v, MontagueFragment.v]: keep shallow/MontagueFragment.v (the imported one), delete extras/Montague.v.
